title: Trombonists: Jimmy Harrison, Jack Teagarden, Lawrence Brown
summary: Greer speaks of trombonists, and calls Lawrence Brown 'Sweetie'.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: Jimmy, good pal of mine. He play up there at the Savoy with Chick Webb. Yeah, he was something else. Jimmy Harrison, Big Jimmy. He big cat about as big as you. Jimmy's a little taller than you, I think. He -- Big Sid the drummer and Big Jimmy, he could play some trombone too. He's something else. I know them guys. We hung out.
He and Jack Teagarden used to hang out together.
Yeah, yeah. Poppa T. I played with him too.
What did you think of Teagarden?

Oh, fine, fine, yeah, he was something else. Poppa T was something else. He played fine, man. Strictly New Orleans Poppa T. I nicknamed him Poppa T. Miff Mole was another trombone player. He's good. He was a studio
man, he could play a trombone, and all of them idolized Lawrence though, when they heard Brown, the top come off, the cap come off.

Lawrence Brown, Lawrence was, out of all our guys, he was the most unassuming guy -- he didn't have them instincts like we had. We called him Sweetie. Ben Webster called him Sweetie. / Sweetie Brown. Yeah, man, Sweetie was something else. He was a heavy lover. He say, hey sweetie come on, man, he didn't drink nothing, didn't smoke, but he was -- with them women, he was all right. Poor Lawrence, nice guy, they all take advantage of him. A nice guy, get the/stick all the time.
